properties.name: A design is named by an id that resolves to a location — never by the path itself
properties.statement:
A DESIGN IS NAMED BY AN ID THAT RESOLVES TO A LOCATION. cap:select-graph-by-id frames it correctly — the server maps id to path — so the id is primary and the path is a storage detail. A surface that treats a filesystem path as the canonical identity forecloses object storage, where the location is a key and the identity rides as metadata.

ADVISORY — Anthony, 2026-08-09, splitting this clause out of rule:per-design-state-is-never-a-process-global and answering the enforcement question for both halves at once (gap:ba21fb8550a81e07): "Split it: clause 1 enforced, clause 2 advice."

WHY IT IS ADVISORY AND ITS SIBLING IS NOT, which is the reason the split was worth making rather than a hedge. The two clauses sit in OPPOSITE positions against the code. The no-globals clause is already satisfied — three runtime process-globals exist and two of them are legitimately process-wide — so a detector for it passes today and its only job is to stop the fourth one. This clause has no compliant surface at all: `--graph-path` is how a server is pointed at a design, `compare_designs` takes `base_path`, `describe_designs` answers about a path, and cap:select-graph-by-id is `planned` with nothing realizing it. An honest detector would therefore fail against the entire existing tool surface on the day it was written, and the only ways to make it green would be to block every build or to attach a check that proves nothing — which is precisely the failure the `enforced` tri-state was introduced to end (dec:does-enforced-default-to-gate-blocking: "a KPP that nothing checks is a comment").

So the flag says what is true: this is the project's rule, confirmed by its author, and no build has been stopped by it because nothing can yet tell compliance from the status quo.

WHEN IT SHOULD FLIP. The honest trigger is cap:select-graph-by-id becoming realized — once a surface exists on which a session names a design by id, "a NEW surface must not take a path as identity" becomes checkable against something other than the whole codebase. Until then this rule does its work at the moment of the decision it would break, which is the same mechanism rule:no-foreclosure runs on and the same reason that rule is also advisory.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY: nothing about WHERE a design is stored, nothing about hosting, and nothing that requires the registry to be built. It only keeps the door open.
